texts.preamble: Tirupati Bakers And Confectioners ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 March, 2025 Author: Pranay Verma Bench: Pranay Verma Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:8449 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Indore Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pranay Verma On The 26th Of March, 2025 Writ Petition No. 10596 of 2025 Tirupati Bakers And Confectioners Through Its Partner Naresh Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others Appearance: Shri Vinayak Balchandani - Advocate for the petitione Shri Mukesh Parwal appearing on behalf of Advocate Ge Order
texts.facts: This petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been preferred by the petitioner being aggrieved by the order dated 17.03.2025 passed by respondent No.1 whereby the appeal preferred by him against the order passed by respondent No.2 suspending his license has been dismissed. 02. On the basis of an inspection conducted at petitioner's premises, samples of confectionery items were prepared and Form 5A were taken. Certain irregularities were found which were in violation of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The license of the petitioner was suspended and the Designated Officer passed an order on 23.01.2025. The same was challenged by the petitioner by preferring an appeal which has also been dismissed by the impugned order.
texts.arguments: 03. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the samples which were sent to the State Food Laboratory for analysis in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:8449 2 WP-10596-2025 report have been stated to be confirming to the norms and were declared fit for human consumption hence the appeal preferred by the petitioner ought to have been allowed. Learned counsel for the respondent/State has pointed out that the fact of receipt of the lab reports has not been brought to the notice of the appellate authority by any of the parties which hence deserves to be directed to reconsider the matter.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 03. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the samples which were sent to the State Food Laboratory for analysis in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:8449 2 WP-10596-2025 report have been stated to be confirming to the norms and were declared fit for human consumption hence the appeal preferred by the petitioner ought to have been allowed. Learned counsel for the respondent/State has pointed out that the fact of receipt of the lab reports has not been brought to the notice of the appellate authority by any of the parties which hence deserves to be directed to reconsider the matter.
